Kids as little as 3 love hiding and seeking and older adults love the memories of hiding and seeking out your playmates from their youth. The game can be played with 2 to 7 players.

This game is beautifully made with hard cardboard of a nice dark looking forest with a stone path. While putting the trees, stump and rock formations together, you will want to put the die under a light so it will glow in the dark for game play. You then place the masks on the Shadowling creatures. The Seeker gets to roll the die and move the lantern, after his eyes are closed, so the other player (s) can hide the little masked Shadowlings.

As the Seeker moves around the board, should any light hit any Shadowling- exposing them, their mask is removed and they are frozen and cannot move until another Shadowling can come and help him. Should all the Shadowlings end up together hiding in the same spot with their masks on, they win. Should the Seeker expose them all, freezing them, the Seeker wins. The room must be pitch black, so the tiny lantern can cast shadows and expose the hiding Shadowlings. A wonderful game of Hide & Seek played in pitch blackness that all ages will enjoy. 5 STARS.

Highlights Hidden Pictures Search Game and Book Love this for my toddler! This comes with two items - a hidden flashlight game and a activity book. The two are independent, so I will review them independently.

The hidden flashlight game is so cool. This one is a 4 paneled game where you stick flashlights into either side's opening and then try to find hidden objects. You can do an "easy mode" or a "hard mode" - the difference is that one type of flashlight illuminates the whole "path" of its light, while the other just has a small "spotlight" circle. At some point, if you play this thing enough, you'll probably memorize where everything is, but they claim 1,000+ different items, so it should be a long while until that happens.

The activity book is nice too, though not atypical of other similar activity books. It's got your expected mix of coloring, connect the dots, spot the differences, etc. But it's a thick and meaty book so would be great for long car trips or dinners. I wish the quality of the pages were a little higher, as ours is already getting abused, but again - not atypical of these kinds of books.

All in all, a great package for some good dedicated board game nights or long trips.
text_fidelity_b: Highlights Hidden Pictures Search Game and Book

PAI TECHNOLOGY Botzees Easy-to-Build 6-in-1 Coding Robots for Kids with Puzzles, Augmented Reality STEM Toy, Ages 4,5,6,7,8,9,10+ Year Old Boys and Girls (App Based) I gave this PAI TECHNOLOGY Botzees Building and Coding - Construction Kit with Puzzles, Augmented Reality to my 7 year old son as a gift from Santa. In comparison to other robot building kits, I wasn't that impressed. First of all, you MUST have an updated iOs or Android phone/tablet. I am unsure if Android has this problem, but if you have an iPhone 5 or 6 and you can't update to the latest iOs, you will not be able to use this robot. Also, since this is an augmented reality app, I doubt that the Kindle Fire will work on this. The camera just isn't powerful enough. I ran into this problem with my son's Fire HD 10 for other AR programs. Next, when you unbox, there are no instructions. You have to go a website to get the instruction manual, which could have been printed on the two cards in the box that say go to the website for a manual. Finally, this does not come with a power source. There is a lithium battery and a USB cable, but you will have to have your own plug. Obviously, many of us will already have various plugs, but to have a designated plug would be nice considering the amount asked for this product.

Overall, my son's interest in this was limited. He's much more interested using his other building toys and finding ways for them to move. I think he feels limited in his creativity. You cannot use this without the App, so any ideas he has of incorporating other mediums to this has him frustrated. It's a nice idea. However, considering that I try to limit his screen time as well it would be nice to have an off screen option to play with this.
text_fidelity_b: PAI TECHNOLOGY Botzees Easy-to-Build 6-in-1 Coding Robots for Kids with Puzzles, Augmented Reality STEM Toy, Ages 4,5,6,7,8,9,10+ Year Old Boys and Girls (App Based)

As well as being fake LEGO it has one other claim to fame.
It is very disappointing.
When companies copy (not be inspired by. I am all for being inspired! this is copying) because of patents, they cannot copy the construct of the bricks. So they end up with bricks that do not push together well, giving models less resilience to being knocked over, picked up or even played with.
Except for the tile pieces. They stick like they were coated in gorilla glue! You may need power tools to get them apart.

Aside from the poor quality of the bricks, what else can be said? Nothing good, sadly. The set designs are primitive. The vehicles are not all on the same scale. Some will not hold the minifigs.
The accessories are another disappointment. Ugly, hard for the minifigs to hold.

If you have a nephew or niece who loves LEGO, and you simply cannot stand this family member, you have found the perfect gift.

Otherwise, keep looking. You will pay more for LEGO, and it is worth every cent!

text_fidelity_a:
Power Wheels Dune Racer, Chrome I figured the Fisher-Price Power Wheels Dune Racer would be a great way to keep my nieces' occupied when they visit. It certainly made them very happy when they saw it! Over all, it's a great power cart and an improvement on the one they have at home, but there are one or two minor issues.
It was delivered in a large box, and since is a 'some assembly required' type of toy, some components were not secured in the box. These parts were in plastic packed within thin foam, along with heavier parts, and had been bounced around in shipping. Because of the way the racer was packed, this meant that there were some scratches on some of the smaller chromed plastic pieces. A minor detail, but some people might not be happy to have a toy arrive in less than pristine shape (also, know that a VERY large box may be just left on your porch or by your garage).
Assembly took the boyfriend about 45 minutes using a screw gun with no issues... but he's pretty good about putting things together. Might take some others a bit longer.
While we tested the battery and found out that it had a little charge right out of the box, for a full charge, you pretty much will have to charge it overnight (about eighteen hours). So yeah, there's a bit of delayed fun-time with the toy. Might be some disappointed kiddies if they see it and then find out they can't do much more than sit in it for about a day.
The decals were tough to peel from the sheet. The wax paper was peeling off along with the sticker due to how thin the stickers were, and they were cut too deep into the backing paper. All in all they were a bit of a pain to put onto the racer - might not be worth it to put them on at all (not sure my nieces care about them, to be honest).
Another minor issue is that the gas pedal is in the middle of the cart, causing the driver to stretch a little to reach (especially when you add that you can't move the seat forward). The shifter was also in the center, as well as directly under the driver’s right knee (at least for my nieces, who are a little more than four years old). So when they were touching the gas pedal, it would sometime shift gears on them, between reverse, low and high. They seem to be learning to be more careful, but still, something to be concerned about when this happened, especially in reverse when they would hit the gas, and their leg would bump the shifter into forwards, causing the cart to lurch in that direction.
A nice thing about the Fisher-Price racer is that it goes well on both grass and on hills with a 30 degree angle. Compared to an older power wheels toddler 6v that the girls have that couldn't manage going up hills, they're having so much more fun (and want to take it home). The seat is comfortable and the racer looks great (scratches aside).
There is no 'brake' to the racer, but once the foot is removed from the gas pedal, it stops.
All in all, the racer is a hit and I'm sure the girls will be begging to come over to use it. One or two features could be better designed (I have to wonder if it's to fit to older kids as well to younger), but on the whole, it's a very nice cart that kids should be able to enjoy for a couple of years (depending on their age).
Overall the kids love it and have a blast with it. Giving 4 stars because of packing, QC issues, and some ergo issues.
text_fidelity_b: Power Wheels Dune Racer, Chrome

text_fidelity_a:
Assassin’s Creed Syndicate Assassin's Gauntlet with Hidden Blade This is so much nicer than the cane sword. It fits on the left hand and the blade ejects with a snick kind of sound, and quite a bit of force. It's spring loaded, and if you look very closely you can see the spring, but I could imagine the "original" was the same. It's heavy leather and has gorgeous detailing. This one is worthy of Comicon or serious cos play.

The "metal" looks aged aged, a little oxidized, and not at all like plastic. It barely feels like plastic when you run your fingers over it, only a bit too warm in the cold weather. The leather looks distressed, and a bit worn, even on the inside by the knuckles. The stitching in the leather is impeccable, and with a great eye for detail. Some of the stitches are a tad longer than others, which happens with hand sewing, not typically with machine stitching. Yes, it was clearly done by machine, but the effect is to look pre-industrial which fits the game perfectly. There is even fake dirt in the spring of the grapple line.

The buckles on top are non-functional. It stays on with velcro straps on the bottom. It fits my small woman hands only barely and I imagine would be fine on a fairly tall man as well.

As with the cane, this is not for kids. The blade is on the sharp side, as is the assassin logo grapple point (I didn't notice in the game that the hook is the logo -- very cool detail). It could do some damage, especially if pointed to the eyes, and the grapple hook is a bit delicate looking. Nothing serious, but handle with some care.
text_fidelity_b: Assassin’s Creed Syndicate Assassin's Gauntlet with Hidden Blade

White Mountain Puzzles The Eighties - 1000 Piece Jigsaw Puzzle [[VIDEOID:b94eac5104dc142a073b662ff11284e3]] I loved this amazing puzzle. The artwork is fantastic! This is a painting of a whole bunch of pictures and other scenes and people from the 1980's. It's based on a painting by Jim Mellet, and his art is amazing! It takes a ton of scenes and people from the 1980's, and turns it into a wonderful painted collage.

The quality of the puzzle is top-notch. The pieces are very thick, and so they fit together well. In my video, you can see that I can actually pick up the entire puzzle, which is usually impossible to do with most puzzles. The backing is a nice blue color, so you can easily tell which pieces are upside down. The border is awesome. The puzzle is surrounded by a red and orange line. This makes the border really easy to put together, and it makes it very easy to identify the edge pieces.

The puzzle is challenging, but it's also very doable. In most puzzles, there's a huge spot of the same color that's very boring, and this puzzle didn't have any of this. I felt entertained and challenged throughout. It's also a great conversation starter, because it has so many iconic people and scenes. I especially liked the Atari, Donkey Kong, Pac-Man, and Mr. T.

Pros:
+Challenging, yet doable
+Fun events and people from the 1980's
+Excellent artwork
+High quality puzzle

Cons:

Ravensburger Empire State Building 216 Piece 3D Jigsaw Puzzle for Kids and Adults - Easy Click Technology Means Pieces Fit Together Perfectly We hit a Waterloo at piece 181 that took days to get past. For some reason the peices became much harder to put in all at once. There are dividers taht happen whenever the building reaches a ledge, and this was one such point. Oddly, it was harder than the rest. The easily frustrated might be tempted to shove it in a box in the darkest part of the deepest closet and pretend it didn't happen. Those who enjoy putting the same twelve pieces in 6,000 times until it sticks will find this absolutely delightful. So not for beginning model builders, but nice for intermediate and advanced. Probably also good for advanced beginner.

It isn't a puzzle in the classic sense. The instructions tell you how many peices to put in, and you put them in by following the numbers. Then you get an embellishment and another group of numbers. It's a model that provides the appearance of a jigsaw.

Overall, I had a lot of fun with it, the resulting model was beautiful, and even though it's sitting on top of an out of the way bookcase, it's gotten many compliments.
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Empire State Building 216 Piece 3D Jigsaw Puzzle for Kids and Adults - Easy Click Technology Means Pieces Fit Together Perfectly

text_fidelity_a:
Winning Moves Games 1223 Kozo, Wood Grain Family game night is a big deal in our house when we’re all together and I have been looking for new games to keep things fresh. We have Jenga, a fun game in its own right, and Kozo on the surface appears to be very similar in concept. It’s a bit trickier, though it’s great fun. The one reservation I have is the sheer number of small parts – easy to misplace or lose if care isn’t taken with storage.

The concept is very similar to Jenga: stack and arrange your pieces and build your tower up without knocking it over. In concept, this is about as simple as it gets. However… Unlike Jenga, there are different sized pieces of different types, and as a result the placement is a lot trickier. Also, there are more rules to gameplay regarding what to place and when, and you don’t necessarily lose when the tower falls as there are multiple rounds to play (if you follow the rule set as specified). Overall, it’s a lot of fun.

My concern is that there are a number of small pieces and these can easily get lost or misplaced. If the tower falls, it doesn’t take much for some of the smaller black cubes to skitter away and end up under furniture where they’re more difficult to track down. This is unfortunately the nature of this game; making the pieces bigger would increase the cost.

Overall, fun game! It takes a little more strategy and effort than Jenga and the replayability is high. Be careful to keep track of the little pieces though.

Monster High Monster Maker In my opinion, kids are born these days innately knowing how to handle technology with their little hands. We first used the [[ASIN:B00IVFCD0Q Monster High Monster Maker]] with an eight year old who guided me through each step. I had already downloaded the software for using on my computer, had installed the included AA batteries, and connected the printer cable. His approach was very different than mine because he wanted to print his design on all the legs, then the arms, then the heads. I wanted to do each of the three dolls as a single being. By inserting the pens which actually can be used to draw freehand, the design is drawn directly onto the doll parts and if you don't like the outcome or grow tired of it, they are erasable. My only complaint about this kit is that two wig caps are included and a single rooted wig whereas the rooted wigs are far superior. The shoes are pretty cute and the dresses are very simple. When I have time, I'll put together some more of the little dresses with fabric scraps.

Keeping all the small parts together is well contained with this set and the [[ASIN:B00LOR4Z3Q Monster High Monster Maker Primary Extension Pack]] is an affordable addition. Because the ink is fairly light when applied to the dolls, there has not been residual color remaining after we've used the eraser to clean them up for refreshed designs. This is a very smart "toy" that is capable of entertaining small groups of children as well as a single designer. By having more dolls on hand, it's a great tool for a birthday party, especially when each child can leave with a doll of their own that they have designed.

Educational Insights Raccoon Rumpus Game, Preschool Game with Dice & Color Matching, For 2-4 Players, Fun Family Board Game For Kids Ages 3 to 5 This is a precious little game that I imagine young children will long remember.

You get 4 cards that have a raccoon in his/her underwear. (There are no bras on the underwear cards, just underwear/panties) The basic raccoon cards all look the same, though. The face on the raccoon is a plastic piece that's raised off the card. The outfit cards have a hole where the face goes, so the outfit cards actually fit right onto the raccoon card.

Your little ones will roll two dice. They will get a color and a piece of clothing to look for. For example, if they roll a red and a picture of pants, they will look for a card with a red pair of pants on it. The child that gets 5 outfit cards first, wins.

So, it's a quick game. My 2 year old has a tiny attention span right now, and there's very few games that hold his attention. This game is a good choice for him. It's teaching him his colors, taking turns, types of clothing, counting. It's a wonderful little game!

It's also fun for my 5 year old, but he is delayed. I imagine the perfect average ages for this game is 2-4 years old. It's pretty simple for an older child.

Overall, this is a very cute game, and I highly recommend it for little ones just learning to play games!

text_fidelity_a:
Mega Bloks TMNT Collectors Krang's Rampage Building Kit We're huge Lego fans in my house, so while it may not be fair, I couldn't help but compare Mega Bloks with Lego. We got a few kits to try out, but otherwise, we've only used Lego in the past(though quite a bit of it). Unfortunately, Mega Bloks has just fallen short, for me, and I wasn't overly impressed(for the most part).

First of all, I've been spoiled to numbered bags. While this kit is divided into separate bags, you have to open all of them and dump them out, because the pieces you need for each step could be in any of the bags. I prefer, if I'm using a kit, to have my steps divided by bags. It keeps thing from getting less jumbled and lost, and it provides great "rest" points. It kind of made me wonder what the point of all the bags were in this set.

Second, these blocks just didn't go together smoothly. Some of them require a great deal of pressure to get attached. They hurt my fingers. I even snapped my finger between two of the blocks at one point trying to get pieces together. (Sad, but true.) My fingers just ache after working with Mega Blocks due to the amount of pressure required to get some of the pieces together. Some of the pieces were incredibly frustrating to get together. Not only that but some of the parts from the final product keep falling off/apart. It took so long to put the thing together(with so much pain) that it almost brings some tears to see parts fall off. ;)

Third, the directions aren't as clear as I'd prefer. Sure, as an adult, I figured things out, but for the average child, the directions just make things harder than they have to be.

When I discovered that Mega Bloks were compatible with Lego, I was really excited. I thought that the block building world could open up to more options for me and my children. We're sticking with Lego, though! It seems more organized and the pieces are more reliable. (They have more of a perfect fit than we've experienced with Mega Bloks.)

In defense of Mega Bloks, though, the little figurines are way cooler, and they have soft parts! IF you are a fan of Mega Bloks, this kit is cool! (I just found it a pain. Literally.)
text_fidelity_b: Mega Bloks TMNT Collectors Krang's Rampage Building Kit

text_fidelity_a:
Star Realms: Deckbuilding Game What can I say? This has quickly become my favorite card/board game for several reasons.

1. It's quick. Many games can take hours to play. We play best 2/3, and it usually takes about an hour. Or: about 20 minutes per game.

2. It's variable. What flops on the first turn can change the whole game, because each player has to react to it. Each player is, of course, also reacting to the other player. This translates into a number of different strategies, so each time you play it, it ends up being 'new' in some way, even if you're playing with the same person. This variability makes it more fun because you can never just 'phone it in'.

3. It's easy to learn. There aren't too many rules, so you can teach it to a new player in a few minutes. Of course, they usually have to play several games before they start winning, but that's just a matter of learning the different strategies involved.

Conclusion: HIGHLY recommended.
text_fidelity_b: Star Realms: Deckbuilding Game

text_fidelity_a: Kiddieland Mickey Deluxe Trike, Ride on My toddler is really into Mickey right now so I just had to get him this trike. It’s adorable and super well made. Assembly was straightforward, thanks to clear and helpful instructions. It took me about half an hour to put together but my toddler was “helping” me so it really wouldn’t take quite that long. I really appreciate the design of this trike since it’s made to grow with your child. It starts out with safety straps, bars that lock in as a secondary way to keep your child in the seat and a handle so you can push and steer. There’s a switch on the front wheel that you slide so it will move without the pedals. Once your child gets big enough to ride alone, move the switch back and the front wheel is controlled by the pedals. The handle is removable as are the safety bars and canopy. I always love finding toys that will get a lot of use since there are so many things that are really only made for short time periods or specific developmental stages then they’re quickly outgrown. This is a wonderful toy and I’m looking forward to helping my son learn to ride it as he grows.

It weighs 1 pound 8.9 ounces (706 grams). It measures 5 1/5 inches across (14cm), 3 1/2 inches (9cm) deep and 4 inches (10cm) at it's height. The sculpting is sturdy. It consists of two solid resin pieces that are attached with 2 very sturdy hinges. The hinges are sturdy enough to support the heft of the lid while it is displayed completely open. It does not tip, nor attempt to close once opened completely. The front features a clasp that has a loop for a lock. All hardware pieces are sturdy, and attached to the Mimic with small screws. I will attempt to edit the review to let you all know the results upon arrival of the lock.

The Conjurer Co Mimic Chest Dice Storage Box is styled and sculpted to be true to Mimic D&D monster lore. The interior bottom really does resemble the obnoxious monster, instead of simply being a storage box. I count this as a plus, as nearly anyone can simply paint a plain trinket box and call it a Mimic. I am especially impressed with the interior sculpting, it's terrifying, especially the sculpted eye inside and 21 teeth inside the top lid. The interior bottom of the Mimic has 25 teeth and sculpted gross Mimic guts. Scary stuff for sure! The exterior painting is quite nice. It does not scratch away easily. I'm happy with the company's paint job, but with it being resin, it could be removed and repainted by anyone wishing to do their own customization or paint job. Conjurer Co. By Merhoff & Larkin is proudly stamped into the resin of the bottom exterior. Each box will have some slight variations, as this is clearly a hand-crafted, hand-painted piece. Personally, I'm a fan of handmade items, and find this box as a very pleasant surprise.

I found The Conjurer Co Mimic Chest Dice Storage Box has exceeded my expectations. I did my own comparison with many other artistic interpretations of a Mimic along with alternative storage boxes. This does the job of easily storing 3 sets of common sized acrylic dice along with serving as a horrifying prop during play. I'm excited to bring The Conjurer Co Mimic Chest Dice Storage Box to the table, it's an impressive hand-crafted prop. Between games, it will make a nice display piece with some other D&D props and figures on a shelf. It's a good value, especially once I made some comparisons between The Conjurer Co Mimic Chest Dice Storage Box, other dice storage boxes and different types of hand-crafted Mimic props.

The Conjurer Co Mimic Chest Dice Storage Box is an ideal, unique gift for any table-top role play enthusiast, figure collector or your beloved local Dungeon Master. It would also serve as a nice gift for yourself. It comes packaged in a small, white cardboard box with an interior lined with 1/2 inch Styrofoam. It would be easy to wrap in paper to present as a gift.

Klutz Felted Friends Craft Kit I purchased this for my cousin's daughter, who at six is considerably below the age recommended. In terms of skill I think she can handle the assembly instructions - one might object on the grounds of the pokey-stabby tool used for the felting, and while she did poke herself a couple times during the install, her parents fared considerably worse.

Speaking of which; she produced a fuzzy friend (the bunny - purple, to be specific) within an hour of trying. The project went well, though her father managed to break two of the needles during the trial-and-error phase, so I'll have to replace those. She seemed to have some fun with it, especially since she was able to assemble the bunny with her parents. There is also a certain amount of observation involved - you have to watch and learn the art of felting, which I think is a good experience for a kid; obviously it didn't take too long, but then my sister was also assisting and she knows all about material/felt/stitching/quiliting and that sort of stuff.

Overall, I would say it makes a good gift. It is, as described, easy to get into and produces a walnut to kiwi-sized fuzzy animal with maybe thirty-minutes of actual work. Probably best for kids over the age of six, though.

Would recommend for gifting to first cousins once-removed.

text_fidelity_a:
Hot Wheels Track Builder Build Your Race Playset Out of all the newer 2016 Track Builder Releases, this in my opinion, is the best! There are multiple ways of setting up various layouts which the manual suggests, and good variety of pieces, though straight track are lacking as usual. The star of this show is no doubt, the duel booster! It's very "next gen-ish", as it looks nothing like boosters that have been around forever. What makes it unique is the way it is set up. There's your usual battery-eating power brick (this uses 4 D cells), but both boosters are independent from the power source. They simply plug in to the battery block, so you can place them away from each other, giving your layout twice the power to shoot your cars around. You don't have to use both boosters, but why wouldn't you? What's more interesting is, the booster's rollers are now vertical, instead of horizontal. When a HW car enters, a single rubber roller grips it from above and launches it out, and both boosters pack a punch! I only wish the connecting cords could have been longer, as you can't place the boosters too far way from each other.

The white support towers are one of the newer pieces found in this series, as they can be placed horizontally or vertically to support tracks. Each tower offers a number of node connections, so tracks can be connected at various heights using the pivot points. The pivot points are brilliant little button-like gizmos that slide easily slide into any track. Now when you snap your track into any of the towers, you can actually rotate and angle your track with much freedom. All in all, it's a very roller coaster-style approach to track building, and a good one at that.

As far as the layouts go, there are a few duel shoot outs as in...gravity drop to booster, through loop, then off to space (hopefully, a carpeted one). These are short lived, 2 second runs but kids will have fun launching their cars simultaneously (this set only comes with one car of course). One interest layout features a continuous run where both boosters work together to continuously shoot your cars through a figure 8 course. Cars zoom around and eventually crash, so it becomes a survivor game. The sample courses won't hold a child's attention for long periods, but they can experiment on their own, and combine the pieces with other sets.

And finally, the box. The new, thicker cardboard box also doubles up as an extra stunt accessory. Perforated cut outs allow tracks to be integrated for even more variety. If your kid rather keep the box, then get ready for a shock: You can actually fit all the pieces back in the box for storage. I know, right?

Overall, this is example of Mattel heading in the right direction.
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Track Builder Build Your Race Playset

text_fidelity_a:
Imagine Meditation Kit for Kids - Award-Winning Mindfulness kit of XL Cards with Calming Guided Meditations for Empowerment, Focus and Relaxation. Great for Parents, Teachers and Therapists. This kit was made to help families like ours. I am a stay at home mom to four kids (11yo and younger). Prior, I was an artist and earned a Special Ed and a Rehabilitation degree. My background has been useful because we ended up a household full of ADHD, severe anxiety, learning and speech disabilities, plus more. We have been using this set for three weeks now and it has proven invaluable. It truly was an excellent find.

We do not own the original set (with the Dove on the box), but I suspect this new version is probably an upgraded improvement of the first box set. It looks very similar, except now there appears have some new (maybe better) ideas and slightly more guidance in this new version. I don't mean to imply this set is a duplicate of the first set, nor am I trying to discourage you from buying both. I simply don't know. I came to the conclusion that these were similar after reading the reviews for the first one. Had I been given the option to chose between the two sets, I would have chosen to start with the newer set I am reviewing here today. Simply because of the changes that were made.

ABOUT THE PRODUCT:

- Most of the cards appear to have between 200 to 300 words. Each activity lasts about 5 minutes per card, give or take. Of course each could be longer or shorter because you get decide how much time you want to spend.

- This newer set has a total of 24 meditation activity cards. 18 of the 24 are guided scenarios. The 18 cards are "story like, short guided imaginary meditation with different scenes that people can imagine themselves taking a part of.” Meaning they ask you to concentrate and imagine yourself in a particular story line (like "walking through the woods" or "stargazing on a warm summer night", for example).
- 6 of those 18 cards mentioned above focus on our senses (touch, taste, etc).
- In addition to the above 18, there are 6 more "positive affirmation" cards. These affirmations address different times of day (morning or bedtime) -or- feelings (anger, stress, etc).

OTHER COMPARISON NOTES:
- From what I can tell, the original set only appears to have 23 guided imaginary "walk through the woods" type scenarios. It does not specifically explore common human experiences that center around feeling or our body.
- The Legend Card is unique to this set. The Legend is more of a guide chart that will help you quickly find the most useful card, depending on the your feelings/needs at the moment­.
- Both sets have the same breathing exercise card.

MY POSITIVES:

- This set is excellent quality. The cards are very nice and are made of a thick paperboard. They are technically laminated, though it wouldn't consider it a plastic waterproof type of covering. It feels more like a wax coating that is water resistant. But it is a sturdy material.
-This truly is an activity for all ages. Kids 6 and younger will probably need guidance. Around 6 or 7, this could probably be an independent activity for most kids. But this mediation set is NOT just for kids. I think pre-teens, teens, and even adults can still benefit from these cards. I wish I made more time to use them myself, tbh.
- These have been excellent in helping everyone in our house decompress and cope with our daily stressors.
- I think this encourages and even teaches how to use our imaginations better (an essential skill!!!).
- It has increases our awareness of self worth. And in a sense, these also teach us to take responsibility for some of our thoughts and feelings too. These activities seem to encourage future motivation and action too.
-This kit is secular and inclusive. Meaning it is not religions in any way. And Many people are represented in the images. The language the cards use, and the activities are age and gender neutral. The suggested scenarios are something anyone can envision.
- And the art is beautiful.

THE NEGATIVES:
- The box is terrible. It's too small. It's impossible to find the one card the Ledged Guide tells you to grab without taking out the entire stack. And it's a pain putting the cards away. I'm going to have to come up with a better storage system.
- There are spelling mistakes, improper punctuation, and unnecessary capitalization. If it had been here or there, I wouldn't have said anything. Nor am I in a position to judge. But it's really bad and does not feel educational.
- The price feels a bit steep initially. However, I think if you make it a goal to give this set a real try and use it for a little while, I think you'll see the $30 price tag actually feels like a good deal.

Overall, I definitely recommend trying this. It is unique and I wish I had know about the original set years ago. But I think this newer set was an even better find. We couldn't be happier. Thank you for reading this ridiculously long review and I hope it helped make your decision easier.
text_fidelity_b: Imagine Meditation Kit for Kids - Award-Winning Mindfulness kit of XL Cards with Calming Guided Meditations for Empowerment, Focus and Relaxation. Great for Parents, Teachers and Therapists.

Under the Baubles Educiro Frozen Ice Princess Castle with Reindeer Sven moveable Toy Building Set for Kids, Girls, and Boys Ages 8-12,(912 Pieces) Anna-Elsa's Toys Gift Ideas This is definitely an adult-level kit that I wouldn't let my little LEGO experts loose on. This one is just for Dad. The intricacy of the design, and the reliance on small, similarly colored bricks is a bit much, even for an adult, so I can't imagine the kids being excited by this.

The kit itself looks marvelous when complete. There are a lot of little hidden spots all over the board that the images can't show in proper detail, but the variety of plant life hidden inside is spectacular. That means that there are a lot of fiddly plant bits that don't quite have a set rotation or feel to them, so perfectionists might have an issue there.

While these are certainly compatible with LEGO, I found a few inconsistencies. Namely, the small 1x1 flats that dot the floor are a micron or two short, and that left me with a few little gaps that were hard to nudge out. Also, I found that I was missing one leaf piece. Not a big deal, and easily replaceable from our collection.

Neither of these are a huge issue - the checkered floor on the one side is certainly not noticable once everything is in place, but it does go to show that the last second checks may not be there the way they are with the major manufacturers.

Everything was properly labeled, and the instructions were above average for a kit of this size and complexity.

The kit says it should take around 8 hours, I clocked mine at 6 and a half.
